analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines ~986-991). It adds a description of a new `darkbloom status` runtime-integrity line. When the coordinator's latest `runtime_status` marked this provider's runtime hashes outdated, the line reports the mismatch count, says the provider is excluded from routing, and recommends `darkbloom update`. The line self-clears after 15 minutes without a `verified:true`. I examined both supplied units: the base excerpt (lines 1683-1888) and the head text (lines 1-399). The head excerpt does not display the added lines, but the patch excerpt covers the hunk, which is complete. The change is docs-only. It adds no code, config, key handling, authorization or data-flow change. It does not touch the TB-002 WebSocket contract, T-041 cache behavior, or the App Attest authorization (TB-011) controls. The documented status line is informational and sourced from a coordinator message on a trusted channel; it does not grant trust. One possible concern is that self-clearing after 15 minutes could mislead an operator into thinking a mismatch was resolved. This is a local status-display matter, and the coordinator keeps excluding the provider while the mismatch lasts. The code that implements this line (StatusCommand+LifecycleDrain.swift or a sibling file) and the coordinator `runtime_status` emission are not in the supplied evidence. A later review pass should confirm that the status line cannot be spoofed locally to hide a real mismatch, and that a stale-clear does not affect routing exclusion. That is unverified and not a finding here. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation-only diff.
